title: Deployment Conformance Crosswalk and Checklist
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

This document provides a cross-functional conformance crosswalk and operational checklist for Redwood Private Deployments that maps common regulatory and customer data-classification requirements to specific deployment controls, packaging expectations, VPC design constraints, day-2 operational practices, and upgrade/rollback guardrails. Use this page during pre-sales technical validation, onboarding acceptance tests, and quarterly compliance reviews.

Scope

- Applies to: VPC-based private deployments, air-gapped on-prem packages, and hybrid control-plane deployments delivered to customers.
- Not covered: hosted API tenant operations, internal SRE-only playbooks (see eng-sre runbooks).

Audience

- Solutions Engineers, Field Engineering, Private Deployments PMs, Security & Compliance, Customer Ops.

How to use this doc

1. Select the customer's regulatory/data profile from the left column of the Conformance Matrix.
2. Apply the mapped controls and validate with the acceptance checklist at the end of this doc.
3. Capture evidence artifacts (audit logs, signed image digests, KMS policy snippets) and link into the customer folder.

Conformance Matrix (high level)

| Requirement / Profile | Network & VPC Controls | Data-at-rest | KMS & Key Management | Runtime Packaging | Day-2 Ops & Telemetry | Upgrade/Rollback Constraint | Acceptance Artifact Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low-sensitivity (internal dev) | Isolated VPC, optional public egress | AES-256 on disk | Redwood-managed key optional | Standard container image | Default telemetry on | Rolling upgrade allowed | Image digest, smoke test logs |
| Regulated PII (EU) | Private subnets, no public egress, egress via customer proxy | Encryption with customer-managed keys | Customer KMS recommended (Cloud KMS/HSM) | Signed images, attestation required | Telemetry sampling limit; PII redaction | Canary first; manual approval for global rollout | KMS policy, attestation report, telemetry config |
| HIPAA / PHI | VPC with strict ACLs, no third-party egress, dedicated subnet for inference | Customer KMS + HSM-backed keys | HSM-backed keys, rotation cadence defined | Air-gapped packaging option | Minimal telemetry; S3-level access logs only | Blue/green with automatic data-plane rollback | Signed SBOM, attestation, access logs |
| Classified / Highly Restricted | On-prem with FIPS-validated components, isolated build & deploy pipeline | FIPS-validated encryption, no external key exchange | HSM + internal KMS with strict split access | Ephemeral boot images, measured boot, attestation | No telemetry off-box; local observability only | Manual, documented upgrade window; rollback appendix required | Firmware attestation, measured boot report |

Notes:
- The rows map common profiles to minimal controls; customer-specific contracts may impose stronger controls.
- For hybrid control-plane deployments, apply control-plane telemetry except where restricted by contract.

Detailed Controls (selected fields)

1) Network & VPC controls

- VPC design must include: dedicated management subnet, tenant inference subnet, and optional shared services subnet.
- Mandatory NSG / ACLs: allow only ports 443 (control plane TLS), 2202 (optional SSH bastion restricted by allowlist), 50051 (gRPC internal), and custom health ports described in service manifest.
- Egress: either blocked or routed through customer-managed proxy/inspection appliance. No direct internet egress for regulated workloads.
- BGP / Cross-region failover: maintain pairwise BGP sessions with route targets documented in network runbook.

Example VPC policy (excerpt):

```
# Minimal security group rules (YAML snippet)
control_plane_sg:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 443
    src: customer_mgmt_cidr
bastion_sg:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 2202
    src: operator_allowlist
inference_sg:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 50051
    src: control_plane_sg
```

2) Data-at-rest and Key Management

- Storage must be encrypted with AES-256 at minimum. For regulated profiles use customer-managed keys (CMKs) in cloud KMS or HSM.
- Key rotation cadence: default 90 days; for PHI/HIPAA recommend 30–60 days depending on contract.
- KMS access control: require separation of duties — CI/CD service accounts must not have unilateral key create/delete permissions.

KMS policy checklist:

- CMK present and validated
- Key rotation policy documented
- Key usage logging enabled and exported to customer audit store

3) Packaging & Image Signing

- All images shipped for private deployments must be signed with our supply-chain signing keys and produce an SBOM. For air-gapped environments produce an offline signed bundle and provide verification steps.
- Image digest must be provided to customer in onboarding artifact.
- Reproducible builds: include exact build recipe and OS package list.

Packaging checklist:

- [ ] Image signed by Redwood CI signature
- [ ] SBOM included (CycloneDX or SPDX)
- [ ] Offline bundle includes signed tarball + verification script

4) Telemetry and Observability

- Default telemetry includes: health pings, model inference latency histograms, error rates, and token counts. For restricted deployments, provide a minimal local-only observability bundle.
- Telemetry must support filtering/sampling at customer request and remove PII at source.

Telemetry options matrix:

- Full (hosted): metrics + traces + logs to Redwood observability (default)
- Filtered (private): metrics to customer endpoint only; traces retained locally
- Local-only (restricted): file-based logs and on-host metrics; periodic collection by ops under customer agreement

5) Day-2 Operations (operational runbook highlights)

- Routine checks (daily): pod health, KV cache hit-rate, GPU utilization, node disk pressure.
- Weekly: snapshot KV caches, verify KMS access logs, run full smoke test via customer API gateway.
- Incident escalation path: SRE on-call -> Private Deployments on-call -> Customer NOC; include runbook link and escalation matrix.

Key day-2 playbook entries:

1. Capacity pressure (GPU contention):
   a. Evaluate batch targets and throttle non-critical routes
   b. Temporarily scale dedicated pool if autoscale enabled
   c. If scale fails, enact model-fallback policy (route to quantized variant)
2. KV cache corruption detected:
   a. Drain traffic from affected replicas
   b. Restore latest consistent snapshot from object store
   c. Reprime caches with warmup traffic using safe prompts
3. Telemetry spike with error rates >5% sustained for 10 minutes:
   a. Switch to degraded model variant
   b. Open incident and run guided debug checklist

Upgrade & Rollback Guidance

Principles:
- Minimize data-plane exposure during upgrades. Prefer canary or blue/green when stateful components are involved.
- Automate preflight checks; require manual approval for production if new packaging changes (e.g., kernel, firmware, FIPS components) are included.

Recommended workflow:

1. Preflight (automated):
   - Validate image signature and SBOM
   - Run integration smoke tests in staging that mirror customer routing (rate-limited)
   - Run KV cache migration dry-run (no write)
2. Canary deployment (1–5% traffic):
   - Monitor latency and error SLO (latency P99 <= baseline + 15% and error rate < 1%) for minimum 30 minutes
3. Gradual rollout (25%, 50%, 100%) with automated health gates

Rollback triggers (examples):
- P99 latency degradation > 50% for 10m AND CPU/GPU saturating beyond expected profile
- Error rate > 5% sustained for 10m on canary group
- Data plane inconsistency (KV mismatch, stateful restore failures)

Rollback procedure (stateful focus):

1. Pause traffic to rolling set
2. Re-deploy previous signed image(s) and rehydrate caches from last successful snapshot
3. Run acceptance smoke tests tied to customer API (see Acceptance Checklist)
4. If rollback fails, escalate to engineering incident + customer war room and enact warm standby (route to hosted/dedicated fallback)

Acceptance Checklist (pre-delivery & post-upgrade)

- Identity & Access
  - [ ] Admin user provisioning completed and tested
  - [ ] Operator allowlist configured for SSH/bastion
- Network & Egress
  - [ ] Private subnets created and verified
  - [ ] Egress path validated (proxy inspection / no direct internet)
- Cryptography & Keys
  - [ ] CMK present (or HSM) and policy attached
  - [ ] Key rotation schedule agreed and documented
- Packaging & Supply Chain
  - [ ] Image digest provided & signature validated by customer
  - [ ] SBOM and build recipe delivered
- Observability
  - [ ] Telemetry mode and sampling configured per contract
  - [ ] Audit logging exported and verified
- Functional Acceptance
  - [ ] Latency P95/P99 and error SLOs validated under capped load (see Test Plan below)
  - [ ] KV cache priming validated and persistence verified

Test Plan (minimal smoke load)

- Run 10-minute capped load at 10 RPS with mixed prompt sizes (short/medium/long). Validate:
  - P95 latency within contract SLA (document SLA value in delivery notes)
  - Error rate < 0.5%
  - Token accounting matches expected limits

Evidence artifacts to collect and hand to customer

- Signed image digest and SBOM (file, path)
- KMS policy snippet and rotation proof (screenshot or policy JSON)
- Attestation report for offline bundle (if applicable)
- Telemetry config manifest showing sampling/filters
- Smoke test logs and SLO graphs

Owner and escalation

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (Priya Shah)
- Delivery owner: Field Engineering lead (assigned per customer)
- On-call: Private Deployments SRE rotation (see eng-sre oncall roster)

Appendices

A. Minimal SLO examples (for acceptance tests)

- Availability: 99.9% (monthly) for dedicated pools; aim for 99.5% for small private installs
- Latency: baseline P95 as observed in staging + 20% allowed during first 24h after rollout
- Error budget: 0.5% monthly for non-critical routes

B. Example rollout command snippets

```
# canary deploy (example)
redwoodctl deploy --image=redwood/private-runtime@sha256:<digest> --canary-percent=5 --health-check=/healthz
```

C. Common customer questions (FAQ)

Q: Can we disable all telemetry?
A: Yes, for the most restricted profiles we provide a local-only observability bundle and a documented process for on-site collection under customer control.

Q: Do you provide HSM integrations?
A: Yes; we support Cloud HSM offerings and on-prem HSMs for classified workloads. Integration verification and acceptance tests are part of onboarding.

D. Change log
